title: The Everything Era: What NAB 2025 Really Told Us About Streaming’s Future
body_html:
What Was Announced

At NAB 2025, Harmonic Inc. highlighted the emergence of a new paradigm in streaming, dubbed "The Everything Era". This concept suggests that the boundaries between traditional broadcast and streaming services are blurring, with a growing trend towards converged workflows that combine the best of both worlds. According to Harmonic, this shift is driven by the increasing demand for more agile, flexible, and scalable content delivery systems that can keep pace with the rapidly evolving media landscape.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The Everything Era represents a significant shift in how broadcasters and streaming services approach content delivery. From a technical standpoint, this means that the traditional silos between different workflows – such as playout, ingest, and metadata management – are being dismantled in favor of more integrated and software-defined architectures. This change has the potential to simplify operations, reduce manual handling, and improve the overall efficiency of content delivery. By automating repetitive tasks and eliminating unnecessary handoffs, The Everything Era promises to deliver faster publishing, more predictable output, and better metadata flow – all of which are critical for maintaining editorial control and meeting tight deadlines. In practical terms, this means that engineering teams will need to reassess their architecture and dependencies to ensure seamless integration with existing MAM, playout, graphics, cloud, and control-room workflows. The key challenge will be to evaluate the change against real-world workflow bottlenecks, rather than relying solely on vendor language. By doing so, teams can determine whether The Everything Era represents a genuine opportunity for simplification and improvement, or simply another hype cycle to be navigated.

Industry Context

The Everything Era is part of a broader trend towards software-defined workflows in the media industry. As streaming services continue to gain traction, traditional broadcasters are being forced to adapt and innovate in order to remain competitive. This has led to a growing interest in converged workflows that combine the best of both worlds – the scalability and flexibility of streaming with the reliability and resilience of traditional broadcast systems. Other approaches, such as cloud-native architectures and containerization, are also gaining traction as media companies seek to simplify their operations and reduce costs. The Everything Era represents a significant milestone in this journey, as it promises to deliver a more integrated and agile content delivery system that can keep pace with the demands of modern media consumption.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For engineering teams, The Everything Era represents a significant opportunity to simplify operations and improve the efficiency of content delivery. However, it also requires a careful assessment of the technical and operational implications, including the potential for increased dependency on cloud-based services and the need for more integrated workflows. To make the most of this shift, teams should focus on evaluating the change against real-world workflow bottlenecks, rather than relying solely on vendor language. This will involve a thorough review of the architecture and dependencies, as well as a careful assessment of the potential benefits and risks. By taking a thoughtful and measured approach, teams can determine whether The Everything Era represents a genuine opportunity for improvement, or simply another hype cycle to be navigated.
